maya: Heads-up — running a long-prefill stress on model-x-13b-int4 on staging and seeing a tiny but consistent divergence after ~65k prefixed tokens. recording quick notes here.

samir: repro steps? full command?

maya:
```
# run on staging GPU pool
rw run --model model-x-13b-int4 --prefill 70000 --prompt-file long_prefill.txt --seed 42 --stream false --kv-cache enabled
```
Log excerpt: 
```
[info] prefill: tokens=70000
[debug] kv_index: last_prefill_pos=65536
[debug] generation[0..10] tokens match
[warn] divergence at gen_step=384 pos=65537 expected=" the" got=" a"
```
small diffs repeatedly reproduce with same seed, only on int4 artifacts.

eva: interesting — does turning off kv-cache make it go away?

maya: yes, disabling KV cache yields no divergence (same run w/ --kv-cache false). also int8 build (model-x-13b-int8) doesn't show the drift.

liam: could be RoPE wrap/position scaling overflow at the quantized kernel boundary. what's the rotary period and how are you applying scaling for long contexts?

maya: rotary_period=4096, but we scale with linear decay after 32k in the runtime (recent change). suspect the combination of int4 rounding + the scaled rotary mix produces tiny phase error that accumulates after crossing 65k.

nina: can you dump kv keys around the boundary? i.e. slices [65520..65560] and compare float32 vs dequantized int4 recon?

maya: done, uploaded diffs to infra run: https://redwood.test/runs/lt-1234 (private). sample:
```
# kv key dotprod diff at idx 65536
float32: 0.0012345
dequantized_int4: 0.0012379  <-- small bias
```
bias magnitude tiny but persistent across layers.

samir: tiny bias * layer_count can amplify token probs. good find. hypothesis: asymmetric quant zero-point + rotary interpolation causes systematic phase shift.

eva: quick tests to isolate: 1) run int4 with no rotary-scaling patch 2) force rotary wrap modulo to original period 3) run with deterministic sampling/topk=1 to make mismatch detection easy.

maya: doing those now. will push results in ~20m.

infra-bot: deploy 2026-03-21T14:12Z: staging/model-x-int4 updated -> kernels/rotary-scaling-v2

liam: also try pre-normalizing kv keys to unit norm before writing back to cache — that'll remove magnitude bias if that's the culprit.

nina: i'll set up a bisect job to find the earliest prefilling length that reproduces (binary search on prefill length). if it starts at ~65536 it's almost certainly a wrap/word-boundary effect.

maya: quick interim results:
- run with rotary-scaling disabled: divergence disappears
- run with int8: no divergence
- run with kv-cache disabled: no divergence
so far points to interaction between rotary-scaling codepath and int4 quantization on cached kv.

samir: actionable: add a unit test for dequantized kv equality across wrap boundary, and a guard in runtime to re-normalize keys when prefill_pos % rotary_period == 0 (or near boundary).

maya: filing issue and will attach logs + minimal repro: https://redwood.test/issue/ML-789

eva: thanks. assign to nina + maya to produce minimal failing test. i'll review the patch for a normalization step.

nina: ack, starting bisect job + adding test harness in tests/longctx/kv_wrap_repro.py. will post PR when green.

maya: thx all. will keep thread updated. :eyes:

liam: :thumbsup:

infra-bot: job/long-prefill-bisect-176666 initiated by nina (id=job-1766).

maya: follow-up — small workaround: for int4 builds, adding a tiny random dithering to quantization seemed to reduce deterministic bias (quick hack). not a fix but helpful for customer-facing staging tests.

samir: good interim. long-term we should avoid any rotary scaling that changes phase continuity across cache writes.

eva: agree. also add a perf test to ensure normalization doesn't add >2% p99 latency.

maya: noted. will include perf numbers in PR.

nina: initial bisect shows first repro around prefill=65520..65550. sharing full trace in PR.

maya: closing loop later today with a minimal patch.
